steps.ordered: CT Abdomen (CT ABD & PELVIS WITH CONTRAST)

assumptions.proposition: Patient has a perforated appendicitis with periappendiceal abscess formation based on CT findings of extraluminal free air, air-fluid collections adjacent to a hyperemic appendix with appendicolith
evidence: Adjacent to the proximal portion of the appendix there is extraluminal free air. A 2.5 x 1.2 cm (601b:36) collection which is predominately full of air is seen slightly anterior to the appendix.
A 0.5 x 0.5 cm (601b:36) appendicolith is seen at the base of the appendix. The appendix is hyperemic and air-filled measuring 1 cm in maximal diameter.

assumptions.proposition: The periappendiceal process involves at least two distinct collections (2.5 x 1.2 cm and 5.7 x 2.6 cm) that may be in continuity, indicating a complex abscess requiring drainage or surgical management
evidence: An additional 5.7 x 2.6 cm (2:63) air and fluid filled collection is seen slightly superior to the appendix and may be in continuation with the previously identified collection.
Secondary inflammation of the base of the cecum and ascending colon is present.

assumptions.proposition: Travel-related infectious or parasitic etiology is now a less likely primary explanation given CT demonstrates classic perforated appendicitis without hepatic or splenic lesions
evidence: The liver is homogeneous in enhancement. No focal lesion identified.

assumptions.proposition: Multi-organ lab derangements (AKI, thrombocytopenia, hyponatremia, elevated bilirubin) likely reflect systemic response to perforation and sepsis rather than a primary systemic infectious disease
Urinary tract pathology is effectively excluded as a primary source given no hydronephrosis, no calculi, and no renal lesions on CT
evidence: No hydronephrosis or hydroureter identified. No renal or proximal ureter calculi.
The bladder is well distended and normal.

previous_order_update.previous_question: Is there an identifiable intra-abdominal or pelvic structural abnormality (e.g., appendicitis, abscess, mass, or other pathology) explaining the RLQ pain, leukocytosis, and systemic derangements?
previous_order_update.effect_on_previous_question: CT fully addressed all structural requirements: appendicitis with perforation and complex periappendiceal abscess confirmed; hepatic/splenic lesions excluded; urinary pathology excluded; extent of inflammation and complications characterized.

discordance.label: concordant
discordance.evidence_stream_2: The appendix is hyperemic and air-filled measuring 1 cm in maximal diameter. Adjacent to the proximal portion of the appendix there is extraluminal free air.
discordance.reason: Leukocytosis and RLQ pain are fully concordant with CT-confirmed perforated appendicitis.
